o1.biggest_strength: It targets the exact leak in the data, gives one clear Agency plan, models the Team cannibalization risk, and tests that risk before launch.
o1.biggest_mistake: It only lightly uses the yearly-billing opportunity, even though yearly uptake is an obvious cheap retention lever.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a clearer, honest yearly-billing treatment within the Agency rollout and tighten the public-launch timing so the invite test does not feel like a hidden plan.

o2.biggest_strength: The revenue math is simple, traceable, and especially useful with the per-1,000-customer table and clear stop rules.
o2.biggest_mistake: It treats Team downgrade risk mostly after launch instead of measuring it in the first test, even though cannibalizing Team is the main danger.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Include Team 8+ customers in the initial test and make the yearly-billing push part of the recommendation rather than a deferred next test.

reason: Both are strong, on-brand, and built on the right data, but Output 1 is safer to run because it tests the biggest risk, Team downgrades, before a public launch. Output 2 has very clean math, but its main cannibalization guard comes too late.
